description: Reunimos diferentes habilidades e perspectivas com um objetivo em comum: explorar ideias, analisar dados e desenvolver soluções inovadoras capazes de gerar impacto na Terra e além dela. Inspirados no espírito dos templários, carregamos valores como união, disciplina, coragem e propósito; e, como interplanetários, voltamos nosso olhar para além das fronteiras conhecidas, explorando novas possibilidades, tecnologias e desafios. Para nós, cada desafio é um território desconhecido a ser explorado e cada integrante tem um papel essencial nessa jornada.
summary:
Rota Adaptada is an agricultural planning application developed by Team Interplários for the NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge, “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” It helps farmers create planting calendars and compare adjustments when delays affect their plans.

The platform combines NASA POWER historical climate data, Brazil’s official ZARC planting conditions, and ISRIC SoilGrids soil estimates. Users confirm their location, select crops and cycle durations, define planting dates, and save a calendar. They can then simulate delays and explore alternatives while preserving the original plan.

Available on mobile and desktop, the application offers guided workflows, downloadable summaries, and local storage for plans and drafts. A demonstration in Vilhena, Rondônia, Brazil, illustrates the planning process.

Transparency is central to the project: missing information is marked as “not evaluated,” historical climate data is not presented as a forecast, and soil estimates do not replace laboratory analysis.

The current version supports scheduling and scenario comparison. Future development will focus on farm-specific evidence and field validation with agronomists and producers. Rota Adaptada aims to turn Earth science data into accessible information for better-informed agricultural planning.
details: Rota Adaptada uses the NASA POWER Daily Point API to retrieve historical precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), maximum and minimum air temperature (T2M_MAX and T2M_MIN), and root-zone and surface soil wetness indices (GWETROOT and GWETTOP) for user-confirmed coordinates. These records support agricultural calendar analysis and comparisons of planting-delay scenarios. Historical observations are not presented as weather or yield forecasts.
